Here’s why: 1. **Honesty in Business (Proverbs 11:1)** – *"A false balance is an abomination to the Lord, but a just weight is His delight."* Dishonesty in pricing undermines trust and integrity, which are values Christians are called to uphold (Colossians 3:9-10). 2. **Breaking Trust (Proverbs 20:28)** – *"Loyalty of friends is a refuge; there is a very trustworthy person who can be trusted."* Overcharging after misleading a customer violates trust, which is foundational in relationships. 3. **Love and Justice (Leviticus 19:35-36)** – *"You shall do no injustice in judgment, in metrics of length, in weights, or in measures. You shall have honest scales, honest weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin."* Fairness in transactions reflects God’s character. 4. **Fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23)** – Honesty is part of the fruit of the Spirit, while deceit contradicts it. While business can be complex, Christians are called to **pursue integrity** (Ephesians 4:25) even in transactions. If the mechanic had simply corrected the mistake transparently, it might have been handled differently—but charging more after misleading the customer aligns with dishonesty. Would you like guidance on how to respond in a similar situation as a Christian?
